results.title: 150 OFWs from Middle East return to Cagayan Valley amid conflict
results.description: TUGUEGARAO CITY, Cagayan — Around 150 overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) in the Middle East have been able to return to Cagayan Valley amid the escalating conflict involving Iran, the United States and Israel, which has also affected several Gulf countries. Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA) Region 2 Director Virsie Tamayao said the returning OFWs were immediately given financial assistance for food and transportation expenses. Many have decided not to return abroad due to security concerns and were provided livelihood assistance to help them establish businesses in the Philippines. Tamayao said OWWA personnel have been deployed almost daily, including weekends, at the Tuguegarao and Cauayan airports to assist returning distressed OFWs, particularly those who are sick or have disabilities. Active OWWA members may receive up to P30,000 in immediate financial assistance and P20,000 in medical assistance for treatment lasting up to six months. Those capable of working may also receive up to P20,000 in livelihood assistance. OWWA coordinates with the Department of Trade and Industry for business training, consultations and monitoring of livelihood beneficiaries. Tamayao said OWWA also assists OFWs facing abuse, unfair treatment, job loss and other difficulties arising from conflicts and unrest abroad through its e-CARES system and coordination with Migrant Workers Offices. Meanwhile, around 3,000 beneficiaries in Cagayan Valley are expected to be selected for the OFW Dependents Scholarship Program for school year 2026–2027 from the 10,000 slots nationwide. Tamayao said 24 new scholars qualified under the Educational Development Scholarship Program this year, while 15 OWWA scholars in the region graduated with Latin honors.

results.title: Nine dilapidated, stinky UV Express units apprehended
results.description: The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) has deployed mystery riders that would focus on UV Express units that are dilapidated, stinky and questionable road worthiness. LTFRB chairman Vigor D. Mendoza II said nine UV Express units were already apprehended since the mystery riders were deployed on Aug. 12 for those that ply the Bulacan-Metro Manila routes. He said the operation stemmed from the complaints of passengers in relation to bad UV Express service in Bulacan. Most of the complaints are poor air-conditioning units, faded markings and unpleasant smell. “Dilapidated, untidy and stinky PUVs have no place in the country’s public transportation system. Hindi na puwede ngayon ang okay pa, either the operators would shape up, or be shipped out,” said Mendoza. He said a show cause order (SCO) was already issued against the nine UV Express operators, which asked them to explain in writing why their franchise should not be suspended or revoked, the violation is in relation to their failure to provide comfortable service to the public. Aside from UV Express, the LTFRB has been targeting taxi, buses, passenger jeepneys and even ride-hailing services with dilapidated, untidy and stinking units. A number of SCOs were already issued in relation to these violations. Mendoza himself has been personally going around Metro Manila to check on the condition of PUVs—his latest inspection resulted in the issuance of SCOs on three PUVs in the Intramuros area in Manila. “We will do everything in our power to compel PUV operators to provide the best service they can give to the Filipino commuters because that is what they committed when they applied for the permit to operate,” said Mendoza. He also urged the commuters to inform the LTFRB of any dilapidated and stinky PUVs that they would come across with, as well as erring and abusive drivers through the LTFRB hotline 1342, or through the agency’s social media accounts.

results.title: Atletico sign veteran Argentinian defender Romero from Spurs
results.description:
Madrid: Atletico Madrid signed 2022 World Cup winning centre-back Cristian Romero from Tottenham on Saturday for a fee reported to be 40 million euros ($46 million) including add-ons.

"(Romero) signs for our club until June 30, 2031," said Atletico in a statement.

The Argentina international -- who was also a member of the robust Argentina side that lost in last month's World Cup final to Spain -- is Atletico's fourth signing this summer after Alejandro Grimaldo, Kang-in Lee and Morten Hjulmand.

The 28-year-old said goodbye to Spurs fans on Friday after five years in north London.

He was named man of the match when the club ended a 17-year trophy drought beating Manchester United to win the 2025 Europa League.

Romero, who incurred several suspensions during his 156 appearances for Spurs, acknowledged "the journey wasn't perfect" in his leaving message, but said he was departing with a "heart full of memories" and "enormous pride".

Romero arrives days after compatriot and fellow World Cup winning defender Nahuel Molina left Atletico for Serie A side AS Roma, for a fee reported to be 17 million euros.

results.title: ‘Bond, trust and understanding have been very strong,’ says Harmanpreet Singh on Manpreet’s influence
results.description: New Delhi, Aug 15 (IANS) India hockey captain Harmanpreet Singh has credited the enduring bond with senior midfielder Manpreet Singh and the presence of experienced players across the squad as key factors in giving the team stability ahead of the FIH Hockey World Cup. Harmanpreet and Manpreet have shared a long journey together, dating back to their junior days, and the India captain believes that years of playing alongside each other have built an understanding that becomes particularly valuable during high-pressure moments. “Manpreet paaji has been our senior. We’ve been together since the juniors. From then until now, that bond, trust and understanding have been very strong. We’ve been playing together for so many years, and I just want to say thanks to him for showing the trust and faith in me,” Harmanpreet told JioStar. That familiarity extends beyond match situations, with Harmanpreet revealing that the group of experienced players often spends time together away from the pitch as well. The India captain said those close relationships have naturally strengthened their communication and understanding during matches. “Even when we go home, during training sessions, we are mostly together, me, Manpreet, Mandeep, Dilpreet. When in camp, we naturally stay together,” he added. For a team preparing to compete at the highest level, Harmanpreet believes such familiarity can make a significant difference when matches become intense. The understanding between the midfield and defence, he said, has developed through years of playing together and allows players to anticipate situations without relying solely on verbal communication. “On the field, the understanding between defenders and midfielders is excellent. We know how to pass in certain situations, how that eye contact works. We stay close in defence too, so there is no communication gap,” he stated. The experience within the squad is particularly notable at a World Cup, where the pressure of knockout-stage hockey can test even the most accomplished teams. Harmanpreet pointed out that several senior members of the current Indian side have already experienced the demands of the tournament on multiple occasions and believes that experience can prove invaluable when the team finds itself in difficult situations. Having senior players willing to take responsibility during crucial moments can help settle the rest of the group and maintain composure. “For Manpreet and Mandeep, this is their fourth World Cup; for me, it’s the third. When a senior player puts their hand up in a crunch situation, it instils confidence in the team,” the India captain said. Harmanpreet also underlined the importance of having experienced campaigners spread across different departments rather than relying on leadership from a single part of the team. He feels that balance gives India multiple players capable of taking charge when required. “I’m glad that in every position we have senior players who can balance the team, Mandeep in the forward line, Manpreet in midfield, and us in defence.” --IANS vi/

results.title: Atletico Madrid sign Argentina defender Cristian Romero from Tottenham
results.description: Madrid, Aug 15 (IANS) Atletico Madrid have completed the signing of Argentina defender Cristian Gabriel 'Cuti' Romero from Tottenham Hotspur, with the 28-year-old centre-back signing a contract until June 30, 2031. Romero joins Atletico after five seasons with Tottenham, where he established himself as a key figure in the club's defence and helped Spurs win the 2024/25 UEFA Europa League. The Argentine defender was named the best player of both the competition and the final as Tottenham secured their first European title in 31 years. A right-footed central defender known for his physicality, anticipation, aggressive tackling and leadership, Romero brings considerable experience to Atletico's backline. Born in Cordoba on April 27, 1998, Romero began his professional career with Club Atletico Belgrano, making his first-team debut in August 2016. He moved to Europe in 2018 to join Genoa before signing for Juventus in 2019. During his time under contract with Juventus, Romero spent the 2019/20 season on loan at Genoa and the following campaign at Atalanta. He was named Serie A's best defender during his season with Atalanta. Romero then moved to Tottenham on loan for the 2021/22 season, with the Premier League club making his transfer permanent at the end of the campaign. He made 156 appearances for Tottenham, scoring 13 goals and providing seven assists across five seasons. At international level, Romero has won 58 caps for Argentina since making his debut in June 2021. He has been an important member of the Albiceleste squad that won the 2021 and 2024 Copa America titles and the 2022 FIFA World Cup. Romero was also part of Argentina's campaign at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, where they finished runners-up. Tottenham, meanwhile, paid tribute to Romero in a farewell message, describing him as “a warrior on the pitch” and highlighting his role in the club's Europa League triumph and his captaincy during the 2025/26 campaign. “A warrior on the pitch, a key part of our Europa League triumph and captain for the 2025/26 campaign. Good luck for your next chapter, Cuti,” The club wrote on X. --IANS sds/
